title: What is the Repo Rate and Why Did the RBI Just Keep It Unchanged?
description: The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for short periods. It's a key tool for the RBI .

faq.q: What is the current Repo Rate in India?
faq.a: As of the latest Monetary Policy Committee meeting on August 8, 2026, the Repo Rate stands at 6.50%.
The six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India decides the Repo Rate. It includes three members from the RBI and three external members appointed by the government.

faq.q: How often is the Repo Rate reviewed?
faq.a: The MPC meets bi-monthly, meaning every two months, to review the economic situation and make decisions on the Repo Rate and other monetary policy instruments.

faq.q: What is the difference between Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate?
faq.a: The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the RBI. The Reverse Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks.

faq.q: Does a Repo Rate cut always mean cheaper loans for everyone?
faq.a: Generally, a Repo Rate cut leads to cheaper loans, but banks also consider other factors like their cost of funds, credit demand, and risk assessment before fully passing on the benefit to all customers.
